papers.summary: Explains low-rank LoRA optima through finite-rank maps induced by frozen activations and trace-norm regularization, without NTK linearization.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses LoRA geometry and nuclear-norm-style regularization. Its empirical support is limited by single optimization trajectories.

evidence.quote: Trace-norm regularization then forces the optimizer to pick a low-rank matrix among all matrices that produce the same observed output.
The current figures show single optimization trajectories without error bars.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: DT-LoRA refreshes a dynamic branch with principal residual-gradient directions outside the current LoRA tangent space while retaining a fixed rank budget.
papers.relevance: Closely matches optimization of low-rank parameterizations and tests language-model fine-tuning under matched trainable-parameter budgets.

evidence.quote: Across ten representative LoRA variants, we show that this tangent-space residual exhibits strong spectral concentration
Under matched trainable parameter budgets, DT-LoRA consistently outperforms LoRA and its variants.

papers.title: DT-LoRA: Reaching Beyond the Tangent Space of Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Ori uses streaming k-PCA to track drifting gradient subspaces during low-rank LLM training. At rank 32 in a 1B LLaMA comparison, its reported optimizer-step peak memory is 0.2487 GB versus 0.3385 GB for GaLore.
papers.relevance: Directly informs the quality–memory–time tradeoff of low-rank gradient optimizers.

evidence.quote: We report validation perplexity after a fixed token budget
at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Studies residual correction for memory-efficient subspace optimization and extends it to Muon. In 1.3B LLaMA pretraining, the reported peak allocated memory is 53.44 GiB for PMRC versus 54.00 GiB for GaLore and 57.77 GiB for AdamW.
papers.relevance: Combines low-rank gradient states, Muon, convergence analysis, and LLM-scale memory measurements.

evidence.quote: we adopt a residual correction framework, which maintains the optimizer states in the subspace and adds the orthogonal residual gradient to the parameter update.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon applies matrix-aware updates to structured factors. Its separate quality runs compare optimizers at fixed factorization, while systems measurements compare memory and step time across model widths.
papers.relevance: Provides measured quality, memory, and speed tradeoffs for structured, memory-efficient LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: Holding the Monarch factorization fixed isolates the effect of the optimizer.
At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: Compares rank measures of language-model fine-tuning updates against random-matrix and matched-fine-tuning baselines, finding that different measures give different readings of the same singular-value tail.
papers.relevance: Directly informs how to assess effective rank and compressibility claims about weight updates.

evidence.quote: Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below.
Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail.

papers.title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline

papers.summary: Idea2Prior combines candidate discovery, identity checks, abstract assessment, citation expansion, and bounded full-text evidence for paper ranking. Its historical Hit@5 comparison favors it on EASY and MEDIUM queries, but not HARD queries.
papers.relevance: The closest match to building an auditable research-digest retrieval and ranking agent.

evidence.quote: The central design separates inexpensive assessment of a broad candidate pool from a bounded examination of document evidence.
The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: The shortlist is drawn from the fixed eligible corpus, not an exhaustive literature search.
Ori’s cited memory figure measures additional optimizer-step peak memory, not full training peak memory.
Monarch-Muon’s large-model systems measurements are separate from its complete quality runs; projection-refresh times for comparator methods are excluded.
Retrieved passages do not establish DT-LoRA’s training-memory or step-time overhead.
Idea2Prior’s comparison uses selected historical runs and includes one convention-based ChatGPT target credit.
